validator: draft 1 passes with no problems, soft points or warnings
keep: The idea is named up front: an insulated supply is joined to earth through its capacitance, and a first fault passes three times one line's healthy charging current, growing with the system.

The picture is the brief's cable that is a capacitor: a feeder with three rows of capacitors to the hull, a cable-length slider, a ten-drives switch, a phasor panel, Healthy / Fault on L1 / Person on L1 and a 480 V check.

The causal chain has no gap: plates charge and discharge, so ωCV flows; healthy currents 120° apart cancel; the fault moves the hull to L1 (i2), L1's capacitance passes nothing, L2 and L3 at 440 V pass 1.73 times as much, 60° apart, adding to 1.73 × 1.73 = 3 times.
Every figure recomputed: X_C 2,650 Ω, 96 / 166 / 287 mA at 1 µF, 192 / 575 mA at 2 µF, 479 mA / 830 mA / 1.44 A at 5 µF, body 190 mA and 36 mA through 1,000 Ω, 480 V check 0.35, 0.60 and 1.04 A.
Each brief misconception has a DO screen with its own hint: capacitor as barrier (2, 6), no other end of the circuit (10), first fault always tiny (8, 11), plus √3 for 3 (11, 12).
Twelve screens: SHOW 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 alternate with DO 2, 4, 6, 8, ending on three mixed puzzles 10 to 12. SHOW screens 64 to 78 words. Recall opener on screen 2 says Still there.
Four footnotes, each on a figure or rule he would look up, at most one a sentence; no source named in a sentence.

faults.where: explain: 'never truly cut off from earth' is true but reads as rhetoric; 'the 30 mA an RCD trips at' overstates: a 30 mA RCD is rated to trip at or below 30 mA.

faults.note: the brief names the two healthy lines' currents adding head to tail, the cause of the threefold sum.
taught mode, no checks; DO screens apply the rule.

faults.fault: talks about the idea instead of teaching it

plain_writing: Several explain sentences run past 20 words: the opening's 'Every cable and winding ... capacitance', 'A capacitor passes ω × C × V, where ...', 'L2 and L3 each sit ...', 'It leaves the supply on L2 and L3 ...', and 'A small system passes milliamps, but a 480 V system ...'. Split each.
Practice uses 'f' in 2π × f × C × V_phase without naming it. Say 'the frequency'.
The bold takeaway is 27 words. Tighten it.
shape: Matches the recommended shape: idea up front, rule in words, worked example with real numbers (practice: 2 µF, 192 mA, 575 mA), misconceptions failing on DO screens, a trade analogy (RCD with many computers) with where it breaks, practice with steps, rules of thumb and mistakes, a sayable recap.
verdict: Rewrite as draft 2 for the long sentences, the RCD wording and the unnamed f; nothing structural.
